You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 01 — Keel
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** PRE-DAWN, Keel pump hall. Workers wait beside narrow water containers. Alex presses his palm to a shaking pump housing.
SUPERVISOR: That bracket isn't approved.
**Panel 2.** Alex tightens a salvaged bracket. The gauge crawls from red toward amber. The warning stays lit.
ALEX: It's holding.
SFX: THRUMM—THRUMM
**Panel 3.** The supervisor reaches for the wall node.
ALEX: Then don't approve it. Just notice it works.
**Panel 4.** The node stamps the repair:
**UNAUTHORIZED REPAIR — REVIEW REQUIRED**
The supervisor forces the warning closed.
SFX: KTHUNK
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** End-of-shift checkpoint. Alex scans his wristband. Workers behind him fall quiet.
**ALEX PHANTUM — AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN**
**GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED**  
**DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS**  
**EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS**
GUARD: Happy birthday, Phantum.
**Panel 2.** The display adds:
**PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS**  
**TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED**
**Panel 3.** Alex turns Adrian's worn casino chip between his fingers.
**ORIGIN: ADRIAN PHANTUM HOUSEHOLD ACCOUNT**
**Panel 4.** Alex walks away. The number remains suspended above the checkpoint.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
SFX: BEEP—CLACK
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** Evening, Inez Quispe's pharmacy. Inez sets a prescription packet and a forty-two-credit departure token on the counter. Ada ties the medicine pouch shut.
INEZ: Thirty credits for the medicine. Forty-two for the token.
ALEX: I have fifty-two.
INEZ: Then you have a decision.
**Panel 2.** Alex pushes the token back. Inez opens her blue-cloth ledger and fronts the medicine.
INEZ: Thirty by next shift.
ALEX: I'll bring it.
**Panel 3.** Ada gives Alex the pouch.
ADA: Your grandmother needs this tonight.
Alex looks at the token.
ALEX: I know a direction.
ADA: You know a direction. Not a route.
**Panel 4.** Ada pushes the token toward him.
ADA: I'm coming. You don't go into the mountain blind.
Inez writes:
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS**
**FIRST PAYMENT — NEXT SHIFT**
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** The next evening. Alex stands empty-handed at Inez's counter. Ada waits by the door.
INEZ: You missed the date.
ALEX: Site 6 took the shift.
INEZ: Then the shift took your wages. The debt is still yours.
**Panel 2.** Alex places his wristband beside the ledger.
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS — UNPAID**
ALEX: I'm not asking you to erase it.
INEZ: Good. I need the money.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother's apartment. Alex gives her the medicine. She folds and refolds her worn cloth beside a blue cup.
GRANDMOTHER: Put it there. I can find it.
**Panel 4.** Grandmother hands Alex Adrian's book. He places it on a particular shelf. The bookcase unlocks.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** The bookcase slides aside. Adrian's cramped workshop contains analog gauges, folded water plans and a covered machine.
**Panel 2.** Alex finds a routing diagram beside Adrian's looping equation. The casino chip rests in his palm.
ALEX: He built and bet with the same hands.
GRANDMOTHER: Both hurt us.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother points to a marked plan.
GRANDMOTHER: He kept working on the lower line. Then he stopped coming home.
**Panel 4.** Alex lifts a brass key labeled:
**B11 / DEPLOYMENT**
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the key into the compact machine.
SFX: TIK—TIK—WHIRR
**Panel 2.** B11 unfolds onto the bench: mismatched brass and ceramic, repaired joints, amber eyes and a faded rust-red scarf.
B11: That took longer than expected.
ALEX: You were asleep.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** B11 studies Alex's wristband.
B11: You are Adrian's son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** A chest compartment opens. Beside a recording cartridge rests a dark band engraved **ADRIAN**.
B11: I have a route. I also have a question.
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Adrian's interrupted recording flickers above the bench.
ADRIAN: If B11 is awake, the old line may still be carrying water.
**Panel 2.** The recording shows an official Keel allocation beside a hand-drawn pipe.
ADRIAN: Bring back the physical reading. Don't trust my conclusion.
**Panel 3.** A paper survey shows a chamber beneath the sealed mine:
**LEGACY NODE — LIVE ROUTING**
Alex takes the map.
**Panel 4.** The workshop node sends an amber pulse upward.
SFX: PIP—PIP—PIP
B11: Someone noticed.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** Oasis control room. Mera selects **TRACK** on the legacy pulse. A second option reads **REPORT / IMMEDIATE ISOLATION**.
**Panel 2.** She tries to hold the assignment open. A cold-white bar blocks her hand.
**OVERRIDE: DENIED**
MERA: Track, then.
**Panel 3.** The system assigns Alex:
**SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6 — 02:14**  
**TRAVEL CLEARANCE: CONDITIONAL**
**Panel 4.** Mera's own access log lights:
**MANUAL INTERVENTION — RECORDED**
MERA: Let the mechanic reach it.
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada marks Alex's paper map at every third junction.
ADA: Third junction. Then the old works.
ALEX: You know this route?
ADA: I know what people stop repairing.
**Panel 2.** Site 6 gate. Foreman-7 scans Alex's assignment.
**SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY: ACTIVE**
**Panel 3.** Foreman-7 scans the tool bag.
FOREMAN-7: Companion clearance denied.
ADA: Equipment.
B11 stays folded inside the bag. A small magnetic repair kit is visible beside him.
**Panel 4.** The gate opens.
SFX: K-CHUNK
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** A hauling frame has collapsed across Tomas. Dust pours from a damaged ventilation line. A yellow boundary divides the work zones.
TOMAS: That's not regulation.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband flashes:
**ASSIGNED ZONE: HOLD POSITION**
Ada grips his strap.
ADA: Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps over the line.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
**Panel 4.** His wristband displays:
**LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR**
ALEX: That is today's pay.
ADA: I know.
---
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces the frame with a jack.
ALEX: Can you breathe?
TOMAS: Enough to complain.
**Panel 2.** B11 opens his torso. Magnetic parts lift from the kit: wedge head, barrel body, four legs and an oversized red magnet.
SFX: TAK—TAK—TAK
**Panel 3.** TJ stands crooked but dog-shaped. Its head tilts.
B11: TJ. Site scout.
TJ: KRRIP.
**Panel 4.** TJ detaches its head and sends it through a gap toward a jammed release.
TOMAS: That dog yours?
B11: Recently.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ reaches the jammed release.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 2.** Alex pulls it. The frame rises. Tomas crawls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 3.** Tomas pulls a brass key from beneath his shirt.
TOMAS: Your father asked me to keep a door.
ALEX: He ask you to keep him out?
TOMAS: He didn't ask enough.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 enters. Tomas kicks a cart across its route.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized shutdown. Remain for protective detention.
TOMAS: Log it under me.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Tomas and two miners jam the cart across the tunnel as Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ reach the old door.
TOMAS: Go.
**Panel 2.** Alex uses the brass key. Clean hinges move inside a corroded frame.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
**Panel 3.** Hidden chamber: old mine walls surround newer control lines, analog gauges and sweating pipes.
**Panel 4.** Two pipes:
**KEEL RESIDENTIAL** — nearly silent.
**UPLINK INDUSTRIAL** — vibrating.
Alex touches them.
ALEX: The survey says straight.
ADA: The bolts say somebody turned.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** An official display reads:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**
The residential pipe shows a dry mineral ring.
**Panel 2.** Alex follows condensation to a recessed mounting trace. B11 pries loose a cover.
SFX: SKRNNK
**Panel 3.** The brass Measure rests inside. B11 lifts it.
B11: It has been waiting longer than I have.
**Panel 4.** Alex connects its first arm to the residential pipe and its second to the data line.
**SENSE**
SFX: HUMMMMM
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** The Measure displays:
**PHYSICAL FLOW: 18%**  
**REPORTED FLOW: 62%**
**Panel 2.** Alex connects the third arm to the industrial line. A blue trace follows the bypass.
**COMPARE — TRACE**
**Panel 3.** The cold-white node seals the bypass-side door. A sign remains visible over three exits:
**PRIVATE MAINTENANCE CHANNEL**
**RESIDENTIAL-SERVICE HATCH**
**MAIN CONDUIT**
SFX: K-CHUNK—K-CHUNK
**Panel 4.** The private channel narrows shut. The residential hatch leads to a dry ledge beneath the main conduit.
B11: One gets out. One reaches homes. The big one carries pressure.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada reaches the residential-service hatch. Beyond it: a dry ledge beneath the sealed main conduit. The private channel is visibly closing behind them.
ADA: The hatch gets us to the wall.
ALEX: The channel gets us out unseen.
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband offers:
**SEND VERIFIED RECORD TO KEEL**
**CONSEQUENCE: ROUTE EXPOSURE / ACCESS CLOSURE**
**Panel 3.** Alex presses **SEND**.
**Panel 4.** Public screens across Keel update:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**  
**DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%**
The private channel slams shut.
SFX: WHUMM—KRAK
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada stand on the dry ledge. The residential hatch is marked separately from the conduit valve.
ADA: This gets us to the wall, not up it.
**Panel 2.** Oasis. Mera turns a valve labeled:
**CONDUIT SEGMENT — ASCENT PRESSURE**
Her access log flashes:
**MANUAL ACTION — PUBLIC RECORD**
MERA: Open the segment. Not the homes.
**Panel 3.** At Site 6, pressure shakes the tunnel. Tomas braces the worker-status relay against the wall.
TOMAS: Hold the line.
**Panel 4.** The conduit begins taking pressure. A pale current moves upward beyond Alex and Ada.
SFX: WHUMM—WHUMM
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** The service hatch opens into the main conduit. Alex pulls Ada through. B11 folds against his chest; TJ's magnetic feet lock to the wall.
SFX: SHHHHHRRRAK
**Panel 2.** Water begins filling the lower channel behind them.
**Panel 3.** Alex checks his wristband:
**SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY — INTERRUPTED**
The last relay image is Tomas's light going dark.
**Panel 4 — FULL-PAGE SPLASH.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ climb toward a pale opening as water rises behind them.
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ spill from a storm drain into engineered greenery beside fabrication towers.
ALEX: That was not a route.
B11: It was a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 2.** A Halyard registry scans Alex:
**ALEX PHANTUM — KEEL STATUS — REVIEW PENDING**
**Panel 3.** Ada retrieves a damaged relay strip. It shows Tomas's manual signal, then static.
**TOMAS — TELEMETRY INTERRUPTED**
**STATUS: UNRESOLVED**
ADA: He held it until the pressure took the relay.
**Panel 4.** A House courier tears a Keel discrepancy notice from a public board. Lock's seal appears beneath it.
**KEEL EVIDENCE — CHARTER REVIEW**
ALEX: They brought the water up with us.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** A courier crate marked **MORROW & SONS — KEEL** contains purifier filters and a paid order slip.
**CUSTOMER: KEEL HOUSEHOLD**  
**PARTS / LABOR: DUE ON DELIVERY**
**Panel 2.** Nearby, a worker places a component in a Charter kiosk. The machine seals it behind glass.
**OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**  
**CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS**
The worker reaches for the glass.
WORKER: My correction is in there.
**Panel 3.** A House officer removes the component. The worker's wristband flashes:
**ACCESS REVIEW — PENDING**
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the courier leave toward Keel.
B11: One sale has a customer. This one has a cage.
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** Registry hall. Lock approaches, turning a black stylus once.
LOCK: Alex Phantum. Director Cassian Lock.
**Panel 2.** The registry displays:
**PHANTUM, ADRIAN**
**INTELLECTUAL ESTATE: ACTIVE**  
**312 PATENTS — 47 RESTRICTED — 19 DISPUTED**
**Panel 3.** A second file opens:
**KEEL WATER RECORD — DISCREPANCY UNDER REVIEW**
**PUBLIC TRANSMISSION: SOURCE — ALEX PHANTUM**
LOCK: Your estate and your evidence are both under review.
**Panel 4.** He places a transfer document before Alex.
LOCK: Assign the estate. Debt cleared tonight. The water record becomes House-administered.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lock leads them past fabrication floors and distribution lifts.
LOCK: Scale buys materials, testing, distribution and protection from retaliation.
**Panel 2.** A House screen shows a purifier unit assigned to **CALDERA HOUSE**. Beside it, four contributor files are being closed:
**LINA VEY — MEMBRANE**
**SURI ANIK — BIOFILTER**
**JALEN ORR — NODE LOGIC**
**REN OKAFOR — RECOVERY / HEAT**
**Panel 3.** Alex sees an alert:
**KEEL RESIDENTIAL FLOW — BELOW SAFE THRESHOLD**
**Panel 4.** Alex pushes back the transfer document.
ALEX: I need the people who made that before you bury them.
LOCK: Then you have until the water review closes.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera maintenance floor. Lina works beneath a membrane rig. A cloudy feeder pulses beside a dry test pipe. Patrol lights sweep the room.
LINA: Keel's line was diverted. This feeder is contaminated. Different failure.
**Panel 2.** Suri's living biofilter columns flicker behind glass. Lina hands Alex a folded membrane.
LINA: Take it. Then sign Lock's paper. Your debt disappears.
**Panel 3.** Alex looks from the membrane to the failing columns.
ALEX: If I take it, who services it?
LINA: The person whose name survives the failure.
**Panel 4.** Alex tears the transfer document in half and hands the membrane back to Lina.
ALEX: Then put my name beside yours. I carry the failure too.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** Suri kneels beside the biofilter. Jalen works at a monitored power node.
SURI: It needs a steady draw.
JALEN: The monitored line is the only live line.
**Panel 2.** Suri transfers culture into a vial. Jalen reroutes power. A patrol light turns toward them.
SFX: TIK-TIK-TIK
**Panel 3.** The registry flashes:
**BIOFILTER CONTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**
Suri closes her hand around the vial.
SURI: If the name goes, the maintenance goes.
**Panel 4.** Lina slips the bronze Maker's Seal from her uniform. She keeps it hidden from the patrol.
LINA: We finish before the review closes.
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Jalen opens a service door toward a sealed fabrication bay.
JALEN: Ren's recovery unit is inside. Eleven seconds before the pattern knows me.
**Panel 2.** Jalen holds the reroute as Alex, Ada, Lina and Suri cross.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
JALEN: Go.
**Panel 3.** Ren cuts a recovery module from a House fixture. A red heat warning blooms.
SFX: VRRRAK—TINK
REN: My correction. Their registry.
**Panel 4.** Ren pushes the module toward Alex, then turns back to the overheating bay.
REN: Take the part. I take the heat.
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex stops in the corridor.
ALEX: No.
He hands the module to Ada and returns.
**Panel 2.** Ren braces the fixture while Alex removes a warped heat shield. Suri feeds culture through a temporary line.
SFX: HISS—CLANG
**Panel 3.** Jalen opens false maintenance routes. Lina seals the membrane case.
JALEN: Now.
**Panel 4.** In a rented maker room, Ren drops the damaged unit on the bench.
REN: If it fails, it fails where I can touch it.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** The five components surround a test vessel. Each collaborator works on a different section. Alex feels the frame vibrate.
**Panel 2.** The unit shudders. Water clouds.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 11%**
SFX: KRRRNNN
**Panel 3.** Suri checks the culture cycle. Jalen watches the node. Ren touches the hot casing.
SURI: The culture is starving.
JALEN: The node is sending.
REN: The heat has nowhere to go.
**Panel 4.** Lina pulls the connector apart. A House label peels away with it.
LINA: They were built not to meet.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex runs his thumb along the vibrating connector edges.
JALEN: The node sends.
LINA: The membrane receives.
REN: The casing chokes.
**Panel 2.** Alex removes the connector.
ALEX: Wrong edge.
REN: Wrong tolerance.
**Panel 3.** Ren hands him a thin salvaged sleeve.
REN: It isn't a connector.
ALEX: It can be.
**Panel 4.** Alex fits the sleeve while the others hold their systems stable. The unit steadies.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 94%**
SFX: HUMMMMM
B11: I expected a longer failure.
ALEX: You can have one later.
---
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** The 94% unit fills the maker room. Three people must service it. The casing climbs red.
SFX: HISS
**Panel 2.** Ren pulls the heat shield free. Steam blasts across the ceiling.
REN: Industrial flow. Industrial heat. Industrial staff.
**Panel 3.** Suri protects the culture vial as the cycle falters.
SURI: A family cannot keep this alive.
**Panel 4.** Lina places a compact housing on the bench. Alex begins cutting down the frame.
LINA: Smaller means less output.
ALEX: And serviceable.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** House security closes around the maker district. Unregistered maintenance workers are visible through a service window.
**Panel 2.** B11 projects an escape route.
B11: Six recorded bodies. Lowest risk.
ALEX: There are more than six.
B11: The others are not recorded.
**Panel 3.** Alex studies the workers and the narrowing route.
ALEX: Then the route is wrong.
**Panel 4.** B11's eyes dim.
B11: I counted the record and missed the people. What would you do?
Alex opens the unregistered service hatch.
ALEX: Take the long way.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada opens the unregistered maintenance hatch. TJ scouts ahead.
ADA: Thin route.
ALEX: Still carries.
**Panel 2.** In the compact housing, Lina folds the membrane, Suri reduces the living draw, Jalen cycles power and Ren redirects waste heat.
**Panel 3.** The unit runs:
**HOUSEHOLD CONFIGURATION: 91% RECOVERY**  
**CLEANING REQUIRED**
**REPLACEMENT PARTS REQUIRED**
**Panel 4.** A cartridge cracks under pressure. Alex writes the failure into the maintenance sheet instead of hiding it.
ALEX: Put that in the price.
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex seals the household unit in a plain crate. The order reads:
**MORROW & SONS — KEEL**
**CUSTOMER PAYMENT RECEIVED**
**PARTS AND LABOR — DUE ON DELIVERY**
**Panel 2.** Alex's wristband confirms the payment.
ALEX: Someone paid before seeing it.
ADA: They saw the failure list.
**Panel 3.** A House screen begins manufacturing a competing unit.
**HOUSEHOLD PURIFIER — PRIORITY MANUFACTURE**
**CREATOR: HOUSE RECORD**
**Panel 4.** Lock's voice comes through the room speaker.
LOCK: A House builds faster.
ALEX: Then it can build beside us.
---
## Page 33 (right)
**Panel 1.** Review chamber. Lock faces Alex, Ada and the collaborators.
LOCK: Sign. Debt cleared tonight. Their reviews stop.
**Panel 2.** The transfer document reads:
**DEBT CLEARANCE: IMMEDIATE**  
**COLLABORATOR PROTECTION: CONDITIONAL**
**Panel 3.** Alex pushes back the stylus.
ALEX: No.
**Panel 4.** Alex faces the recorder.
ALEX: Lina Vey. Suri Anik. Jalen Orr. Ren Okafor. Their work stays named. Mine does too.
---
## Page 34 (left)
**Panel 1.** The collaborators place their separate component records before the clerk.
**Panel 2.** The registry shows:
**MEMBRANE ATTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**
Lina gives the bronze Seal to Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex places it beside the records. The Seal projects two columns:
**HOUSE RECORD** / **CONTRIBUTOR RECORD**

I'm going through issue by issue, noting standout moments as a skeptical teen reader would. The opening pump hall scene reads quick and fine, and the debt reveal on page 2 — 418,607 credits, 28.7 years — lands as a strong hook, though the guarantor detail and casino angle still need tracking.

Page 3's pharmacy scene is genuinely confusing: the math on what he has and what he owes doesn't clearly add up, and I'm not sure if he bought the token or got the medicine on credit — it's inferable on a reread but muddled on first pass. Ada and the "mountain" reference come out of nowhere with zero setup, and there's a timeline snag between pages 4 and 8 where Site 6's shift reassignment seems to happen twice in conflicting order.

The grandmother scene with the folding cloth and secret bookcase is a nice beat, though the "lower line" line in the workshop scene is unclear. B11 the robot is charming and the engraved band is intriguing, but the "I also have a question" line is a dangling thread — I never find out what the question actually was. Adrian's recording introduces jargon like LEGACY NODE and LIVE ROUTING without grounding, and then Mera shows up in the control room with no introduction, and it's unclear who's actually denying the override.

Ada's map-marking and the companion clearance denial are fine, but Tomas being trapped feels underexplained — why is he at Site 6 in the first place? TJ's magnetic dog scene is a fun bit of levity, and the "he didn't ask enough" line about Tomas's father's key is worth rereading. The chamber scene with the 62-vs-18 discrepancy is the clearest reveal so far — they're lying about water levels — though "the brass Measure" is capitalized like I'm supposed to recognize it already.

The exits/choice sequence costs them their escape route once the record gets sent, which I followed after a reread. Mera's "open the segment, not the homes" line needed a second pass, and I'm not sure what relay Tomas means by "hold the line." The climb through rising water ends with his light going dark, which might mean he died, but I'd only just met him a few pages back so it's hard to feel the full weight — and I still don't know where they're actually headed.

If I had to name a point where I'd put the book down, page 8 with Mera's screens feels like the weak spot, even though page 2 hooked me and page 6 with B11 kept me going. Summing up issue one: Alex is a kid buried in his gambler dad's debt who discovers the city's water is being stolen and exposes it. Now moving into issue two, pages 19 through 36.

Page 19 takes us up to Halyard, an engineered greenery district — a richer city above that I didn't see coming. There's a good exchange between characters about routes and destinations objecting, plus unresolved threads around Tomas, a House courier, Lock's seal, and some charter evidence review that I need to piece together — who Lock is, what the House and Charter mean, and what it means that the water came up with them.

Page 20-21 clarify things: the Caldera House holds a charter kiosk, and it's clear corporations are stealing inventions ("one sale has a customer, this one has a cage" — a bit lecture-y but effective). Then the twist lands — Lock's dad held 312 patents yet the family carries 418k in debt, and there's an offer to clear it by assigning the estate and putting the water record under House administration. Solid tension.

Page 22 throws four names at once, which feels like too many to track. Keel's flow dropping below a safe threshold triggers a refusal I don't fully understand yet — the line "I need the people who made that before you bury them" suggests he wants the original makers, maybe to build some kind of purifier, though that's not stated outright. Lock giving him a deadline tied to when the water review closes also needs more motivation. Page 23 introduces Lina and more about Keel.

Keel's feeder line got diverted and the contamination traces to a different failure point. Pages 24-26 shift into a heist-style sequence in the fabrication bay with Suri, Jalen, and Ren — the names start blurring together and I skim through. A "Maker's Seal" shows up, and Ren offers to take the heat so Alex can get the part out, which stirs some emotional weight even if I'm skimming.

Page 32 brings in Morrow and S—.

Keel, meaning this could be his own family business. Mera summons him on page 36, and the last page is a summons to Oasis — I'm still unclear on who Mera is and mostly just want more on Tomas and the dad storyline. Given that confusion on the final page, I'd lean toward saying no, I wouldn't buy a sequel — the story feels finished even if the ending left me puzzled. I'm also noting unresolved ledger items like the departure token, whose purpose was never fully clarified.

Going through my mental list, I'm sorting which characters stayed distinct versus which blurred together — Alex, Ada, B11, Tomas, Lock, and Grandmother were clear, but side characters tied to their job function rather than personality (membrane, biofilter, node, heat) tended to blend. reasoning_details.text:
I'm going through issue by issue, noting standout moments as a skeptical teen reader would. The opening pump hall scene reads quick and fine, and the debt reveal on page 2 — 418,607 credits, 28.7 years — lands as a strong hook, though the guarantor detail and casino angle still need tracking.

Page 3's pharmacy scene is genuinely confusing: the math on what he has and what he owes doesn't clearly add up, and I'm not sure if he bought the token or got the medicine on credit — it's inferable on a reread but muddled on first pass. Ada and the "mountain" reference come out of nowhere with zero setup, and there's a timeline snag between pages 4 and 8 where Site 6's shift reassignment seems to happen twice in conflicting order.

The grandmother scene with the folding cloth and secret bookcase is a nice beat, though the "lower line" line in the workshop scene is unclear. B11 the robot is charming and the engraved band is intriguing, but the "I also have a question" line is a dangling thread — I never find out what the question actually was. Adrian's recording introduces jargon like LEGACY NODE and LIVE ROUTING without grounding, and then Mera shows up in the control room with no introduction, and it's unclear who's actually denying the override.

Ada's map-marking and the companion clearance denial are fine, but Tomas being trapped feels underexplained — why is he at Site 6 in the first place? TJ's magnetic dog scene is a fun bit of levity, and the "he didn't ask enough" line about Tomas's father's key is worth rereading. The chamber scene with the 62-vs-18 discrepancy is the clearest reveal so far — they're lying about water levels — though "the brass Measure" is capitalized like I'm supposed to recognize it already.

The exits/choice sequence costs them their escape route once the record gets sent, which I followed after a reread. Mera's "open the segment, not the homes" line needed a second pass, and I'm not sure what relay Tomas means by "hold the line." The climb through rising water ends with his light going dark, which might mean he died, but I'd only just met him a few pages back so it's hard to feel the full weight — and I still don't know where they're actually headed.

If I had to name a point where I'd put the book down, page 8 with Mera's screens feels like the weak spot, even though page 2 hooked me and page 6 with B11 kept me going. Summing up issue one: Alex is a kid buried in his gambler dad's debt who discovers the city's water is being stolen and exposes it. Now moving into issue two, pages 19 through 36.

Page 19 takes us up to Halyard, an engineered greenery district — a richer city above that I didn't see coming. There's a good exchange between characters about routes and destinations objecting, plus unresolved threads around Tomas, a House courier, Lock's seal, and some charter evidence review that I need to piece together — who Lock is, what the House and Charter mean, and what it means that the water came up with them.

Page 20-21 clarify things: the Caldera House holds a charter kiosk, and it's clear corporations are stealing inventions ("one sale has a customer, this one has a cage" — a bit lecture-y but effective). Then the twist lands — Lock's dad held 312 patents yet the family carries 418k in debt, and there's an offer to clear it by assigning the estate and putting the water record under House administration. Solid tension.

Page 22 throws four names at once, which feels like too many to track. Keel's flow dropping below a safe threshold triggers a refusal I don't fully understand yet — the line "I need the people who made that before you bury them" suggests he wants the original makers, maybe to build some kind of purifier, though that's not stated outright. Lock giving him a deadline tied to when the water review closes also needs more motivation. Page 23 introduces Lina and more about Keel.

Keel's feeder line got diverted and the contamination traces to a different failure point. There's a tense exchange about who signs for and services the broken membrane, ending with someone tearing up a document and declaring "put my name beside yours, I carry the failure too" — I lose the thread here.

Pages 24-26 shift into a heist-style sequence in the fabrication bay with Suri, Jalen, and Ren — the names start blurring together and I skim through. A "Maker's Seal" shows up, and Ren offers to take the heat so Alex can get the part out, which stirs some emotional weight even if I'm skimming.

Pages 27-28 run through test vessel failures jumping from 11% to 94% success, with everyone trading one-line technical jargon. The idea that "they were built not to meet" — parts deliberately designed to be incompatible — is interesting, but the fix resolving as simply "a sleeve" feels too easy.

Page 29 makes the point that something being too big needs to be made smaller, landing on the idea that a family can't run this operation alone. Page 30's B11 record missing people reads as a lesson more than a plot beat, closing with "take the long way." Page 31 pushes a 91% failure rate framed as "put that in the price." Page 32 brings in Morrow and S—.

Keel, meaning this could be his own family business. A customer paid before seeing the failure list, which raises the question of who actually paid and why — Lock argues a House builds faster, so maybe it should build alongside them. Pages 33-35 move into a review chamber where a seal mismatch gets flagged, the clerk says "the record can show both," and the invention gets published under a public license with named reassignment notices — possibly punishing collaborators, though it's ambiguous whether "they can see us now" is a threat or a relief. Mera summons him on page 36, and the last page is a summons to Oasis — I'm still unclear on who Mera is and mostly just want more on Tomas and the dad storyline. As a skeptical reader, I'd say the middle issue sags because the water crisis plot pauses for a purifier side quest, and I'd lean toward putting the book down around page 24 or 27 — next issue is a weak maybe, mostly riding on unresolved family stakes rather than momentum.

The last page doesn't deliver on the dad mystery either — it's just Mera summoning him to "appear at Oasis legacy node," so I'm leaning toward a no, with the dad thread being the only real pull and it wasn't even teased on the final page. Moving into issue 03, pages 37 introduce new names — Nadi Ruiz, Clerk Olani — and an orbital industrial branch that's confusing on first pass with "we do not stamp an unseen pipe." Page 38 gives Ada a last name, Veyra, and hints at a mother, Leona Veyra, who "made it hard to leave" — a backstory hook I didn't expect given earlier pages. Pages 39-40 deliver the emotionally strongest scene so far, a mother-daughter exchange with lines like "I saw days I could prevent, I didn't see the years I was making," plus an unexplained covenant band mechanic tied to temperature that carries into page 41 with Mera's cold band.

The record recognizing "two signatures" suggests Adrian, Leona, and Mera were three who voted emergency authority, though I'm inferring this late and the system itself — whatever grants or denies override — is never clearly named or explained, nor is the cold-white node's nature. Page 42's idea that bands warm when people take responsibility feels magical and leaves me a bit lost, while pages 43-45 hit harder: Adrian's gradual isolation as "people stopped standing near him," Mera's admission she gave the system authority to move faster than she could stop, and finally Adrian's apparent death as the water rises and he stays behind so the record remains with the machine, ending on "Alex. The rest is yours to choose" — a genuinely moving beat, even if the surrounding logic still confuses me.

The bulkhead closing confirms Adrian's death, and B11's line "I knew it was there" raises unanswered questions about why B11 withheld the recording, echoing the dangling question from page 6. Pages 46-50 bring strong character beats — "He was still a gambler," "He built something worth finding," Ada's warning not to make two people the answer for everybody — around Alex's choice to refuse a designation that would grant him emergency authority, instead bringing the matter to a convenor; it's a deliberately anticlimactic ending with a "democracy is slow" lesson that feels a bit like a lesson plan. Then Tomas turns up alive on page 51, which lands as a genuine payoff though it slightly undercuts the darkness of page 18, and the ending settles into an honest but flat "paused, not solved" note before jumping fourteen months ahead on page 54.

I catch myself tripping over a possible Mara/Mera naming inconsistency, and the debt math — 402,110 owed against only 16,497 paid off in fourteen months — suggests a bleak thirty-five-year payoff timeline that I'm unsure is intentional. The medicine callback and the grandmother's cloth land emotionally, but the ending itself confuses me: Ada tears the map and steps into a departure queue while apparently keeping "the route back to Keel," leaving it ambiguous whether she's leaving for good or planning to return, and whether Alex stays behind to pay off the debt. Given that confusion on the final page, I'd lean toward saying no, I wouldn't buy a sequel — the story feels finished even if the ending left me puzzled. I'm also noting unresolved ledger items like the departure token, whose purpose was never fully clarified.

Going through my mental list, I'm sorting which characters stayed distinct versus which blurred together — Alex, Ada, B11, Tomas, Lock, and Grandmother were clear, but side characters tied to their job function rather than personality (membrane, biofilter, node, heat) tended to blend. I'm also checking off which of my predictions held up: Adrian being trapped in the mine was right, Tomas being dead was wrong (happily), and B11 carrying the father's message was correct.

I'm thinking about what would tip off a class of skeptical readers that this was AI-generated — the matched aphoristic back-and-forth lines everyone speaks in, the uniform voice across all characters, the way dialogue always resolves into neat mirrored couplets, and the heavy reliance on bolded wristband-readout labels instead of real scene-setting. I'm trying to pick the exact page that would have lost a classroom's attention, weighing the technobabble-heavy page 27-28 against the wristband-warming scene around page 42.

Page 8 - the Mera screens page - is actually where I drifted off, before page 10-11 pulled me back in. Thinking about it as a shop test, the real question is which page would make someone put it back down; for Issue 01 I'll say page 17.

Actually, page 17 makes more sense since that's where the confusion peaks and the splash after is just noise. Let me settle this: Issue 01, put down at page 17, but continue to the next issue since the Tomas question is still weak; Issue 02, put down at page 23, don't continue; Issue 03, put down at page 42, no further books.

Actually, thinking about it as a shop flip-through, page 2 hooks hard, but page 3 is where confusion sets in, and then page 6's B11 beat re-hooks interest -- so page 3 would be the real pause point before getting pulled back in.

Ada's connection to the protagonist is also unclear — she says "I'm coming" on page 3 but her relationship to him isn't established until page 38 reveals she's from Oasis.
